steps.title: Biological and oxidative
steps.body: Fino and Manzanilla age under flor, biological ageing, giving pale, dry, tangy wines at 15%. Oloroso is fortified to 17%, never has flor and ages oxidatively, turning dark brown with walnut, toffee and spice, yet stays dry. As water evaporates, Olorosos concentrate, reaching 20% or more.
steps.highlight: Fino under flor; Oloroso with air

steps.title: Between the two
steps.body: Amontillado starts as Fino under flor, then the flor dies or is killed by fortifying to about 17%, and the wine ages oxidatively. It combines Fino's tang with Oloroso's nuttiness. Palo Cortado is rare: it starts under flor but loses it early, then ages oxidatively, giving Amontillado's aroma with Oloroso's body.

steps.prompt: Match each Sherry to its ageing.
steps.explanation: Biological and oxidative ageing create the range of dry Sherries.

steps.title: Sweet Sherries
steps.body: Pedro Ximénez grapes are dried in the sun until almost raisins, then fortified, giving black, syrupy wines with over 400 g/l of sugar. Moscatel is made similarly. Cream Sherry blends Oloroso with sweet wine; Pale Cream blends Fino with sweetening. These blends are sweet; the dry styles are not.

steps.explanation: Cream Sherry is sweetened. Fino, Oloroso and Amontillado are naturally dry.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Fino and Manzanilla age under flor; Oloroso ages with air
Amontillado and Palo Cortado combine both
Pedro Ximénez and Cream are sweet styles
